curated.instructions: omr/instructions/42037-1-1.pdf (the off-roader, the book marked 1, steps 1-54); omr/instructions/42037-1-2.pdf (the book marked 2) builds the alternate model

functions.does: Pushed along, the rear wheels run the inline four-cylinder engine in front of the seat: the rear differential's 28 tooth crown drives a 20 tooth bevel gear on a shaft running forward under the seat, and a 16 tooth gear on it drives the crankshaft's 16 tooth gear through a 16 tooth idler, so the four pistons pump up and down, about 1.4 times per turn of the wheels.
functions.source: book: the engine's steps 1-11 (pages 17-20, crankshaft drawn 1:1), steps 28-34 (engine fitted, the gears behind it, pages 20-26), the rear module's steps 2-4 (differential, pages 32-33), steps 39-41 (rear module joined, pages 50-52)
functions.note: the gear count is read from the model

functions.does: The rear differential lets the two rear wheels turn at different speeds; with the car lifted, turning one rear wheel turns the other the opposite way.
functions.source: book: the rear module's steps 2-7 (differential and the drive shafts with their constant velocity joints, pages 32-35)

functions.does: The black gear on top of the roll cage behind the seat steers the front wheels (hand of god steering): its vertical shaft turns, through bevel gears, a long shaft running forward under the car to a 12 tooth gear on the front steering rack, and the rack's links turn both front hubs.
functions.source: book: front module steps 5 (the rack, page 10) and 17-21 (hubs and links, pages 12-14); step 25 (the gear on its vertical shaft, page 47); steps 39-41 (the long shaft joined, pages 50-52)

functions.does: The front wheels each have independent suspension: each steering hub rides between an upper and a lower suspension arm, with a yellow shock absorber, and moves up and down, steering as it goes.
functions.source: book: front module steps 6-27 (arms, hubs and shock absorbers, pages 5-16; the arrow on step 26 swings the shock absorber into place)

functions.does: The rear wheels each have independent suspension: each hub rides on two pairs of arms with a shock absorber, and the drive shafts' constant velocity joints let it move up and down while driven.
functions.source: book: the rear module's steps 5-23 (pages 34-45); inferred: that it's meant to move

functions.does: The shock absorbers' springs hold the car up and spring back.
functions.source: book: front module step 26, rear module steps
functions.skip: springs only matter under force; the suspension moves freely without them

functions.does: The steering wheel in front of the seat turns freely; it isn't linked to the steering.
functions.source: inferred: from the model, the steering wheel sits on a pin, and the book draws no link to the steering

questions.question: Is the steering wheel really unlinked?
